shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Floating layers only: sheets and dialogs, popovers and menus, toasts, the phone tab bar, and the phone's quick-add circle.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: A thumb or segment raised above its own track: the selected segment of a segmented control and the switch thumb.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: A field's focus state, paired with an ink border. It marks state, not elevation.

shadows.name: tile-glow
shadows.purpose: Background, not a shadow: lights a KPI tile's top-left corner; --tile-tint is the tile's own pastel at about 22%.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on every control, app and website alike: ink on the canvas and on ivory; lime in the dark zone, the website's slabs and black cards included. State, not elevation.

shadows.name: slab-tuck
shadows.value: .slab + .slab::before { position: absolute; inset-inline: 0; top: -64px; height: 64px; z-index: -1; background: inherit } inside the isolated .site-root
shadows.purpose: Depth device, not a shadow: a website slab that follows another reaches 64px up behind it, so its color fills the first slab's lower corners and the two read as stacked sheets.

shadows.name: closing-scrim
shadows.purpose: Background, not a shadow: the Command Black wash over the website's closing call photo, so its white type reads; the website's only gradient.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Entrances and the check-in settle: sheets, toasts, the settle keyframes.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Color, background, border, and shadow transitions on buttons, fields, tiles, and toggles.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Pressed state of buttons and circles.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.value: 220ms ease-out-expo; slides up from translateY(32px) and opacity 0

motion.name: sheet-in
motion.value: 240ms ease-out-expo; slides up from translateY(32px) and opacity 0
motion.purpose: Sheet and dialog entrance; the scrim fades in over 150ms.

motion.name: meter
motion.purpose: Meter and chart bar width or height changes.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition to 1ms; toasts and state changes still appear.

motion.name: arc-drift
motion.value: requestAnimationFrame; startOffset advances 0.028px per ms (about 28px/s) plus 0.9 x the page scroll since the last frame
motion.purpose: The ball's arc: the academy's words drift along the lob and run with the page's scroll (backward when it scrolls up), only while the arc is on screen and the tab is visible. Reduced motion, or no IntersectionObserver: the words hold still.

motion.name: reel-travel
motion.value: translate3d(-progress x overflow, 0, 0) on a sticky 100dvh stage inside a section 100dvh + overflow tall
motion.purpose: On court, from 1024px with motion allowed: the photo reel travels sideways exactly its own overflow while the page scrolls down. Otherwise a snap-x scroller with one keyboard stop.

motion.name: proof-nudge
motion.purpose: A proof card's up-right arrow on hover, brightening from Court Mist to Court White.

narrative.overview:
CoachMan is a calm, premium CRM for courts. Every app screen splits into two zones: a black command panel that holds navigation and the live list (today's sessions, the client worklist, who owes), and a soft-gray daylight canvas where the selected session or client opens as rounded white cards. Lime is the single signal across both zones. It lights whatever is live, selected, or the next action, so a coach glancing at a phone between games finds "now" without reading.

Headings and figures are large and light; everything a coach acts on is regular or medium weight and at least 36px tall, mostly 44px or more. Status speaks in soft pastel pills that always carry ink text. Depth is tonal (gray canvas, a lighter folder panel, white cards), and shadows appear only on things that float. Containers take generous 22–32px corners, and every control is a pill or a circle. People appear as initials on soft tints unless the coach uploads a photo. There is no stock or illustrative imagery, and in the app the lime BallMark is the only sport motif.

The visual authority is a reference the user pinned: the Dribbble shot "Microsoft Dynamics CRM – Lead Relationship Management Platform" by Jack R. for RonDesignLab, translated from sales to coaching. It replaced a themed "Court Lines" build and a plain "clean and light" plan, both rejected; the system refuses flat admin tables and sport-themed costume. Where the reference sets white text on pastel pills, CoachMan sets ink, because task surfaces have to read in outdoor sun.

The academy release carries the same world to the people around the coaches. The **family portal** is the calm register: the command panel becomes a black header block that holds the academy's own logo tile and name, the page title, and (on laptops) the navigation as pills; the work sits on the gray canvas as white cards, with lime spent on one thing per screen (the next session, the amount due). The **enrollment wizard** is an Operate flow in the academy's frame: the dark panel holds the academy, the tier, and the steps; one white card holds one question. The **rates sheet** prints the live catalog as a plain letterhead document. An academy brings only its name, logo, words, and photos (its team's portraits, a cover, and its own court photos); the CoachMan palette is never recolored for it.

The **academy website** (`/a/<slug>`: the landing page, Enroll now, and Meet the team inside one site frame) is where the system changes register, because it is the academy's public face for families and players deciding whether to train there. After the Wispr Flow landing page the user pinned, it is a calm, generous Persuade surface built from CoachMan's own materials so it stays in the family: Command Black, ink, lime, violet, and Figtree, set on a ball-tinted ivory ground instead of the gray canvas, with full-width black slabs whose large corners stack like sheets, one court-green slab that carries the coaches' proof, outlined pills and buttons, and an EB Garamond display for its headlines. Its signature is the ball's arc: the academy's own programs, days, and times ride a pickleball's lob across the first screen and drift as the page scrolls. Every word, photo, and figure on it comes from the academy's own data, and it refuses the sports-academy template (a dark full-bleed hero photo with a centered slogan, three icon features, plan columns, a testimonial carousel). Its tokens and rules hold inside the website (`.site-root`) only; the staff app, the family portal, the wizard, and the rates sheet keep the system above.
keyCharacteristics: Two zones: a black command panel (icon rail plus list column) beside a soft-gray canvas of white cards.
Lime marks live, selected, and primary, and nothing else.
Figtree throughout the app: light (300) for headings and figures, tabular numerals for every compared number; the academy website adds an EB Garamond display for its headlines.
Pastel status pills with ink text, never white.
Tonal depth; shadows only on floating layers.
22–32px container corners (the website's slabs grow to 64px); pills and circles for every control.
Records open into fused folder tabs over a lighter panel, with lavender and lime bentos beside them.
Touch-first sizing: 44px controls, 48px check-in circles, 52px action circles.
One world, four audiences: staff (command panel), families (black header block), visitors (the academy website: ivory ground, stacked black slabs, a serif display), applicants (wizard frame).
A visible keyboard focus everywhere: a 2px ring at 2px offset, ink on the canvas, lime in the dark zone.

rules.name: The Lime Is Now Rule
rules.body: Lime marks what is live, selected, or the primary action: the active rail circle, the selected tile, the action circles, the checked-in toggle, the primary bento. It never labels a category, a tag, or a chart series; categories take the pastels.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Pastel Rule
rules.body: Every lime and pastel fill carries ink (#111111) text and icons, never white. This is a deliberate accessibility deviation from the reference, whose pills set white on pastel: white on Owes Coral reads at about 2.8:1, ink at about 6.8:1.

rules.name: The Connection Color Rule
rules.body: Sync Orange speaks only about connection state (offline, syncing, a change waiting to sync), and nothing else wears it.

rules.name: The One Lime Block Rule
rules.body: A screen holds at most one lime block, and it is the thing to act on now: the live session (Today), the next session (the family's Home), the amount due (Pay), the featured tier (Enroll now). Offers that sit beside it (turn on reminders, renew for next month) are white cards with a lime icon circle, never a second lime slab.

rules.name: The Ivory Ground Rule
rules.body: The website stands on Ball Ivory and never shows the gray canvas or a white card. Ivory surfaces are told apart by a ruled edge (Ivory Rule) and Ivory Wash wells; weight comes from black slabs and black cards.

rules.name: The Court Proof Rule
rules.body: Court Green speaks only for the academy's own evidence: its coaches' highlights and certifications, what one real package includes, and whether it is enrolling now. It never fills a button or decorates a section.

rules.name: The Light Heading Rule
rules.body: Across the app (staff, family portal, wizard, rates sheet), every heading and figure from 22px up is set at weight 300 with slight negative tracking (-0.01em to -0.03em). Bold (700) does not exist in this system; in the app the wordmark (22px, 500) is the only large text that isn't light. The academy website follows its own Serif Headline Rule below.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Every number a coach compares (times, counts, credits, money) is set in tabular lining numerals.

rules.name: The Serif Headline Rule
rules.body: On the website, EB Garamond sets page, section, and card titles, the coaches' highlights, and the footer's headings, always at its regular weight (400); Figtree sets every control, body line, label, price, schedule, and number. The serif never appears in the app or on a button.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Headline Rule
rules.body: A website headline written with a clause break (a comma, semicolon, colon, or dash, with at least two words on each side) sets its opening clause in Pewter and the rest in ink: "Train with purpose," then "play with joy". Any other headline stays ink; the page never inserts a break of its own.

rules.name: The Two-Zone Rule
rules.body: In the app, night tones belong to the command panel and its phone forms (the header block and the tab bar); the canvas, the folder panel, and white cards hold the work. A component that lives in both zones ships two tones, a charcoal tile in the panel and a white card on the canvas, never a dark card on the canvas. The academy website has no canvas: its black slabs and black cards on ivory are native (see The Stacked Slab Rule).

rules.name: The Thumb Floor Rule
rules.body: Controls start at 44px: buttons and icon circles 44px, fields 48px, check-in toggles and rail circles 48px, a record's action circles 52px. 36px is the one smaller step, for secondary actions inside cards, sheets, bentos, and toasts. A text link set apart from prose (a footer link, a contact line, "All" in a card head) keeps its look and gets an invisible 44px tap area.

rules.name: The Current-in-View Rule
rules.body: A row that scrolls sideways on phones (folder tabs, filter chips, announcement lists) always opens with its current item in view, and a navigation marks exactly one item as current.

rules.name: The Flat Card Rule
rules.body: Cards sit flat; tone alone separates white from gray. A resting element declares its edge once, with a 1px line or a shadow, never both.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Pop means "this floats above the page". Lift is the only other shadow, and only for a thumb or segment raised above its own track. Cards, tiles, and panels never cast one.

rules.name: The Drawn Edge Rule
rules.body: On the website an edge is drawn once, as a ring or a rule: Ivory Rule between ivory and ivory, ink (white on black) around what a family acts on, and a 2px ink rule around the questions box. A slab or card there never casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Step-Down Radius Rule
rules.body: A shape nested in a container takes a smaller radius than the container: a 32px panel holds 24px list tiles and 22px KPI tiles; a 28px card holds 22px wells and 16px controls.

rules.name: The Stacked Slab Rule
rules.body: A slab spans the full width with large corners all round (32px, 48px from 640px, 64px from 1024px). When one slab follows another, the second reaches 64px up behind the first, so its color, not the ivory, fills the first one's lower corners and the two read as stacked sheets. Slabs belong to the website alone.

rules.name: The Proof Rule
rules.body: A credit count or a balance is a button that opens its proof: the credit ledger or the client's statement.

dos: Do split every app screen into the two zones: the night command panel (84px rail and 328px list column on desktop, a black header block on phones) and the gray canvas of white cards.
Do reserve lime (#daee63) for live, selected, and primary: current navigation, the selected tile, action circles, the checked-in toggle, the primary bento.
Do set every pastel and lime fill with ink (#111111) text and icons.
Do set the app's headings and figures from 22px up at weight 300: record titles 44px and page titles 40px from 1024px, both 32px on phones.
Do give every compared number tabular lining numerals (`.num`).
Do open records into folder tabs that fuse into the Folder Gray panel, with the lavender and lime bentos in a 340px column from 1280px.
Do keep controls at 44px or more (fields and check-in toggles 48px, action circles 52px), and use the 36px small button only for secondary actions inside cards, sheets, bentos, and toasts.
Do confirm a check-in with the lime fill, the 220ms settle, and an ink toast that offers Undo.
Do use Lucide icons at 16–24px, with a 1.75 stroke in navigation.
Do show people as initials on a soft wash unless the coach has uploaded a photo.
Do show an academy's logo as uploaded, on a white tile, and keep the CoachMan palette around it unchanged.
Do spend lime once per screen in the family portal (the next session, the amount due); make offers white cards with a lime icon circle.
Do keep the academy website's way in on its first phone screen: the lime Enroll now in the nav and the hero while the academy takes requests, else Message us.

Do introduce people on the public pages with 4:5 half-body portraits (else the square photo, else initials on a soft wash), the name and title beside or under the image, never on it. On phones a coach's own card leads with a full-width portrait and the rest of the team scrolls sideways; faces in a stack stay circles.
Do keep a visible keyboard focus ring on every control: ink on the canvas and on ivory, lime in the dark zone (the website's slabs and black cards included).
Do give a text link set apart from prose a 44px tap area, and open a sideways-scrolling row with its current item in view.

Do set the academy website on Ball Ivory (#fbfbf0) with full-width Command Black slabs whose corners grow from 32px to 48px (640px) and 64px (1024px), and give the coaches' proof the one Court Green slab.

Do set the website's page, section, and card titles in EB Garamond at 400 (the hero 96px and section titles 64px from 1024px), two-toned only on a written clause break, and keep every control, body line, and number in Figtree.
Do build every website section from the academy's own data and leave out a section with nothing real to show; show what's included from one real package, never a blend.
Do let the ball's arc move only while it is on screen, and hold it still under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use lime to mark a category, a tag, or a chart series; categories take the pastels.
Don't put white text on lime or on any pastel, even though the reference does.
Don't set any app text at weight 700, or an app heading of 22px or more above weight 300. On the website the serif runs at 400, and only the footer wordmark (800) goes past 600.

Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading, and don't uppercase labels. A field label above its value is data, not a kicker; a status pill or a date line above a title is a kicker (put it under the title).
Don't add a colored side stripe to a card, row, or alert.
Don't use gradient text; the KPI tile's corner glow is the system's one decorative gradient (the website's closing scrim is there for legibility, not decoration).
Don't shadow a card, tile, or panel, and don't give a resting element both a 1px line and a shadow.
Don't use icons from any set but Lucide, or glyphs and emoji as icons.
Don't put a dark card on the app's gray canvas or a white card in the command panel; on the website, black cards on ivory are native and white cards don't appear.
Don't introduce a hex outside the `@theme` tokens in `src/app/styles.css`; declare a new color there first.
Don't use stock or illustrative images of people.

Don't reintroduce the rejected themed costume ("Court Lines") or flat admin tables; the BallMark is the app's only sport motif, and the ball's arc (with its dotted path in the closing call) the website's.
Don't stack two lime blocks, or recolor any part of the system to an academy's brand colors.
Don't set a dismissal ("Not now", "Cancel") as an underlined link beside a button; it is a ghost or white button.
Don't mark more than one link in a navigation as the current page.
Don't carry the website's ivory, court green, serif display, slabs, or outline and violet buttons into the staff app, the family portal, the wizard, or the rates sheet.
Don't use Court Green for a button or for decoration; it carries only the academy's own proof.
Don't give the website the sports-academy template: a dark full-bleed hero photo with a centered slogan, three icon features, plan columns, or a testimonial carousel.
